newsitem.title: DUBAI: Former BCCI affiliate gives first result in years.
newsitem.headline: Former BCCI affiliate gives first result in years.

text.p: A former affiliate in the United Arab Emirates of the failed Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI) has reported its first results since BCCI collapsed amid allegations of massive fraud in 1991.

The financial statements of Union National Bank (UNB) -- called Bank of Credit and Commerce (Emirates) until August 1991 -- show that the bank made a 74.72 million dirham ($20 million) profit in the five years and six months to June 30, 1996.
This compares to the 52.98 million dirham profit in the year to end-December 1990.
A copy of the results, approved by shareholders on Saturday, was obtained by Reuters on Sunday.

"The events that unfolded in 1991 had a profound impact upon Union National Bank. However...our bank has come out of this period much better positioned and stronger than before," UNB chairman Sheikh Nahayan bin Mubarak al-Nahayan said.

BCCI, with assets of $24 billion and operations in 71 countries, was closed down by central banks worldwide in July 1991 with debts of more than $12 billion when evidence of massive fraud and money laundering was unearthed.

UNB said the Abu Dhabi government, BCCI's majority shareholder, recently acquired the failed bank's 40 percent stake in UNB. The rest is held by UAE nationals, the Dubai government and the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority.
In the UAE there were about 45,000 BCCI creditors owed nearly five billion dirhams. Small depositors started receiving repayments earlier this month.

Sheikh Nahayan said since 1991 UNB's management and operations had been strengthened, a new credit policy and administration procedure adopted, and a new audit system introduced which "now ensures the highest standards of internal audit discipline".
He said the bank was also working to create more transparency and improve disclosure and would now conform to International Accounting Standards in reporting its results.
